items.title: Readers are said to 'bark' at a text when
options: they read too loudly.
there are too many repetitive words.
they are discouraged from using their imagination.
they have difficulty assessing its meaning.

items.title: The text suggests that
options: pictures in books should be less detailed.
pictures can slow down reading progress.
picture books are best used with younger readers.
pictures make modern books too expensive.

items.title: University academics are concerned because
options: young people are showing less interest in higher education.
students cannot understand modern academic texts.
academic books are too childish for their undergraduates.
there has been a significant change in student literacy.

items.title: The youngest readers will quickly develop good reading skills if they
options: learn to associate the words in a text with pictures.
are exposed to modern teaching techniques.
are encouraged to ignore pictures in the text.
learn the art of telling stories.

items: It is traditionally accepted that children's books should contain few pictures.
Teachers aim to teach both word recognition and word meaning.
Older readers are having difficulty in adjusting to texts without pictures.
Literacy has improved as a result of recent academic conferences.
